- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive or recently neutral; prices tend to correct downward after spikes.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows recent downward momentum; model tends to ignore downside risk.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects sharply downward.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the middle of the forecast horizon, especially when sentiment is mixed or recently positive.
- Lagged sentiment influence: if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly; delay in correction leads to overestimation.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days (days 1–7) when sentiment is strong, then undercorrect later (days 15–30) when sentiment weakens.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment flips — model often continues trend even when sentiment signals reversal.
